overview: The Parthian Empire, ruled by the Arsacid dynasty from 247 BCE to 224 CE, held Iran and Mesopotamia between Rome and the steppe for nearly five centuries. Its armored lancers and horse archers, its great noble houses and its grip on the Silk Road made it Rome's only equal in the East.

items.text: The Parthian shot: horse archers turned in the saddle to shoot behind them at full gallop.
At Carrhae in 53 BCE, horse archers and cataphracts, riders and horses in scale armor, destroyed a Roman army under Crassus.
The empire sat astride the Silk Road; Chinese silk reached Rome through Parthian middlemen who kept the two ends apart.
Envoys from Han China reached the Parthian court in the 110s BCE, and in 97 CE the Han envoy Gan Ying got as far as the Persian Gulf.
Zoroastrian, Greek, Babylonian and Jewish communities kept their own cults, and the kings styled themselves friends of the Greeks on their coins.
The Arsacids claimed descent from the Achaemenid king Artaxerxes II.
The Sasanians inherited Parthian cavalry, provinces and great noble houses.
Parthian, a Middle Iranian language written in its own script, was still used in the Sasanian royal inscriptions.

fall.text: Ardashir I of Persis defeated and killed the last Arsacid king, Artabanus IV, at Hormozdgan in 224 and founded the Sasanian dynasty.
